title: Surface Area of Combinations of Solids: The Hidden Interface Principle
description: Master the fundamental principle of combined surface areas: when two solids are joined together, their touching interface surfaces disappear inside and CANNOT be painted or touched. Therefore, Total Surface Area is the sum of the EXPOSED curved surface areas, NOT the sum of their individual total surface areas.
key_concepts: The Hidden Interface Principle: TSA of combined solid ≠ TSA of Solid 1 + TSA of Solid 2! Touching base faces are hidden inside and must NOT be included
Cone Mounted on Hemisphere (Toy): TSA = CSA of Cone + CSA of Hemisphere = πrl + 2πr²
Slant Height of Cone: l = √(r² + h²)
Cylinder with Two Hemispheres (Capsule): TSA = CSA of Cylinder + 2 × (CSA of Hemisphere) = 2πrh + 4πr² = 2πr(h + 2r)
Cubical Block Surmounted by Hemisphere: TSA = TSA of Cube - Area of Circular Base + CSA of Hemisphere = 6a² - πr² + 2πr² = 6a² + πr²
Hemispherical Depression Scooped Out: TSA = 6a² - πr² + 2πr² = 6a² + πr² (Identical surface area whether surmounted or scooped out!)
subtopics: Deconstructing composite 3D objects into elementary curved components
Calculating cone slant height l = √(r² + h²)
Worked Example 1, Example 2, Example 3 from NCERT

worked_examples.given: Playing top consists of a cone surmounted on a hemisphere (Fig. 12.4). Total height H = 5 cm. Base diameter d = 3.5 cm ⇒ radius r = 3.5 / 2 = 1.75 cm. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Total Surface Area to colour = CSA of hemisphere + CSA of cone = 2πr² + πrl.
Height of cone h = H - r = 5 - 1.75 = 3.25 cm.
Slant height of cone l = √(r² + h²).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A playing top composed of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone.
Total height of the top, H = 5 cm.
Diameter of the top, d = 3.5 cm (Fig. 12.4).
Radius, r = 3.5 / 2 = 1.75 cm = 7/4 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
The total surface area to be coloured.

FORMULA USED:
Total surface area to colour = Curved surface area of hemisphere + Curved surface area of cone
TSA = 2πr² + πrl = πr(2r + l)
where:
- Height of cone, h = Total height - radius = 5 - 1.75 = 3.25 cm = 13/4 cm
- Slant height of cone, l = √(r² + h²)

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute the slant height l of the conical part:
l = √(r² + h²)
l = √((7/4)² + (13/4)²)
l = √(49/16 + 169/16) = √(218 / 16) = √218 / 4
Since √218 ≈ 14.76:
l ≈ 14.76 / 4 ≈ 3.7 cm.

Step 2: Compute CSA of Hemisphere:
CSA(Hemisphere) = 2πr² = 2 × (22 / 7) × (7 / 4) × (7 / 4) = 77 / 4 = 19.25 cm².

Step 3: Compute CSA of Cone:
CSA(Cone) = πrl = (22 / 7) × (7 / 4) × 3.7 = (11 / 2) × 3.7 = 5.5 × 3.7 = 20.35 cm².

Step 4: Total Surface Area to Colour:
TSA = CSA(Hemisphere) + CSA(Cone)
TSA = 19.25 + 20.35 = 39.6 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
πr(2r + l) = (22/7) × (1.75) × (3.5 + 3.7) = 5.5 × 7.2 = 39.6 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 39.6 cm² ].

worked_examples.given: Cube edge a = 5 cm. Hemisphere diameter d = 4.2 cm ⇒ radius r = 2.1 cm. Hemisphere mounted on top face of cube (Fig. 12.7). Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Total Surface Area of block = Total Surface Area of cube - Base area of hemisphere + CSA of hemisphere
TSA = 6a² - πr² + 2πr² = 6a² + πr².
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Edge of the cubical block, a = 5 cm.
Diameter of the surmounted hemisphere, d = 4.2 cm.
Radius of hemisphere, r = 4.2 / 2 = 2.1 cm.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.7).

TO FIND:
Total surface area of the composite block.

FORMULA USED:
The base of the hemisphere is glued to the top square face of the cube, hiding that circular contact area, while the curved dome of the hemisphere is exposed:
TSA of Block = Total Surface Area of Cube - Base Area of Hemisphere + Curved Surface Area of Hemisphere
TSA = 6a² - πr² + 2πr²
TSA = 6a² + πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Total Surface Area of the cube:
Area_cube = 6a² = 6 × (5)² = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

Step 2: Compute net additional area contributed by the hemisphere:
Net addition = CSA(Hemisphere) - Base Area(Hemisphere)
= 2πr² - πr² = πr²
= (22 / 7) × (2.1)²
= (22 / 7) × 4.41
Since 4.41 / 7 = 0.63:
= 22 × 0.63 = 13.86 cm².

Step 3: Compute Total Surface Area of the block:
TSA = Area_cube + Net addition
TSA = 150 + 13.86 = 163.86 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
6 × 25 = 150. (22/7) × 2.1 × 2.1 = 13.86. 150 + 13.86 = 163.86 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 163.86 cm² ].

worked_examples.given: Toy rocket: cone on cylinder (Fig. 12.8). Total height = 26 cm. Cone height h = 6 cm, cone base diameter = 5 cm ⇒ r = 2.5 cm. Cylinder height h_cyl = 26 - 6 = 20 cm, cylinder base diameter = 3 cm ⇒ r' = 1.5 cm. Conical part painted orange, cylindrical part painted yellow. Use π = 3.14.
worked_examples.formula:
Slant height of cone l = √(r² + h²).
Orange area (Cone) = CSA of cone + Base area of cone - Base area of cylinder = πrl + πr² - πr'² = π[rl + r² - r'²].
Yellow area (Cylinder) = CSA of cylinder + Base area of cylinder = 2πr'h_cyl + πr'² = πr'[2 h_cyl + r'].
worked_examples.calculation:
Orange area = 63.585 cm².
Yellow area = 195.465 cm².
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Orange area = 63.585 cm², Yellow area = 195.465 cm²
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Entire rocket height = 26 cm.
Height of conical part, h = 6 cm.
Radius of conical base, r = 5 / 2 = 2.5 cm.
Height of cylindrical part, h_cyl = 26 - 6 = 20 cm.
Radius of cylindrical base, r' = 3 / 2 = 1.5 cm.
Use π = 3.14 (Fig. 12.8).

TO FIND:
(i) Area painted orange (conical portion).
(ii) Area painted yellow (cylindrical portion).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Slant height l of the conical part:
l = √(r² + h²) = √(2.5² + 6²) = √(6.25 + 36) = √42.25 = 6.5 cm.

Step 2: Area painted orange:
The conical part has its curved surface exposed, plus the ring-shaped base projecting beyond the cylinder:
Orange Area = CSA of cone + Base Area of cone - Base Area of cylinder
Orange Area = πrl + πr² - πr'²
Orange Area = π [ rl + r² - r'² ]
Orange Area = 3.14 × [ (2.5 × 6.5) + (2.5)² - (1.5)² ]
Orange Area = 3.14 × [ 16.25 + 6.25 - 2.25 ]
Orange Area = 3.14 × 20.25 = 63.585 cm².

Step 3: Area painted yellow:
The cylindrical part has its curved surface exposed, plus its bottom circular flat base:
Yellow Area = CSA of cylinder + Base Area of cylinder
Yellow Area = 2πr' h_cyl + πr'²
Yellow Area = πr' [ 2 h_cyl + r' ]
Yellow Area = 3.14 × 1.5 × [ (2 × 20) + 1.5 ]
Yellow Area = 4.71 × 41.5 = 195.465 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
Orange: 3.14 × 20.25 = 63.585 cm². Yellow: 4.71 × 41.5 = 195.465 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ Orange = 63.585 cm², Yellow = 195.465 cm² ].

worked_examples.given: Cylindrical bird-bath with hemispherical depression (Fig. 12.9). Cylinder height h = 1.45 m = 145 cm. Radius r = 30 cm = 0.3 m. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula: Total Surface Area of bird-bath = CSA of cylinder + CSA of hemisphere = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A cylindrical bird-bath with a hemispherical depression at one end.
Height of the cylinder, h = 1.45 m = 145 cm.
Radius of the cylinder and hemisphere, r = 30 cm.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.9).

TO FIND:
Total surface area of the bird-bath.

FORMULA USED:
Total surface area = Curved surface area of cylinder + Curved surface area of hemisphere
TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Convert all units to centimetres:
h = 1.45 m = 145 cm
r = 30 cm.

Step 2: Substitute into formula:
TSA = 2πr (h + r)
TSA = 2 × (22 / 7) × 30 × (145 + 30)
TSA = 2 × (22 / 7) × 30 × 175

Step 3: Simplify by dividing 175 by 7:
175 / 7 = 25
TSA = 2 × 22 × 30 × 25
TSA = 44 × 750 = 33000 cm².

Step 4: Convert to square metres:
1 m² = 10000 cm²
TSA = 33000 / 10000 = 3.3 m².

[ROUGH_WORK]
2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 0.3 × (1.45 + 0.3) = 2 × (22/7) × 0.3 × 1.75 = 2 × 22 × 0.3 × 0.25 = 44 × 0.075 = 3.3 m².
Boxed Answer: [ 3.3 m² (or 33000 cm²) ].

common_misconceptions: Adding TSA of cube (6a²) and TSA of hemisphere (3πr²): This double-counts the hidden circular contact face and ruins the calculation!
Subtracting the hemisphere volume when calculating surface area of a carved depression: Carving a depression INCREASES the total exposed surface area by +πr², never decreases it!

title: Volume of Combinations of Solids: Additive Conservation & Liquid Displacement
description: Understand the additive conservation principle of volume: unlike surface area, volume is strictly additive and subtractive. Total volume of a composite solid is simply the algebraic sum of the individual component volumes (or total volume minus carved volume for cavities). Master liquid displacement in vessels.
key_concepts: Volume Additive Invariant: Volume is always conserved; Total Volume = Volume(Solid 1) + Volume(Solid 2)
Cavity Volume: When a cavity is scooped out, Remaining Volume = Original Solid Volume - Cavity Volume
Cylinder Volume: V = πr²h
Cone Volume: V = 1/3 πr²h
Sphere Volume: V = 4/3 πr³
Hemisphere Volume: V = 2/3 πr³
Archimedes Liquid Displacement: Volume of water overflowing = Total volume of submerged solids
subtopics: Additive volume property for combined solids
Subtractive volume property for hollowed cavities

worked_examples.given: Cuboid dimensions: length l = 15 m, breadth b = 7 m, height h = 8 m. Half-cylinder: diameter d = 7 m ⇒ radius r = 3.5 m = 7/2 m, length (height) L = 15 m. Space occupied by machinery = 300 m³. 20 workers occupy 20 × 0.08 = 1.6 m³. Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.12).
worked_examples.formula:
Total volume of shed = Volume of cuboid + Volume of half-cylinder = (l × b × h) + (1/2)πr²L.
Net air volume = Total volume - (Machinery space + Workers space).
worked_examples.calculation:
Total volume = 984.375 m³.
Air available = 682.775 m³.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Total volume = 984.375 m³, Air in shed = 682.78 m³
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Cuboid: length l = 15 m, breadth b = 7 m, height h = 8 m.
Half-cylinder: diameter = 7 m ⇒ radius r = 7/2 = 3.5 m, length L = 15 m.
Space occupied by machinery = 300 m³.
Number of workers = 20; each occupies 0.08 m³.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.12).

TO FIND:
(i) Total volume of air that the shed can hold.
(ii) Net volume of air when machinery and workers are inside.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of cuboidal portion:
V_cuboid = l × b × h = 15 × 7 × 8 = 840 m³.

Step 2: Compute volume of half-cylindrical portion:
V_halfcylinder = (1 / 2) × πr² L
= (1 / 2) × (22 / 7) × (7 / 2)² × 15
= (1 / 2) × (22 / 7) × (49 / 4) × 15
= (11 × 7 × 15) / 8 = 1155 / 8 = 144.375 m³.

Step 3: Total volume of the shed:
V_total = V_cuboid + V_halfcylinder
V_total = 840 + 144.375 = 984.375 m³.

Step 4: Compute occupied volume:
Volume of machinery = 300 m³
Volume of 20 workers = 20 × 0.08 = 1.6 m³
Total occupied volume = 300 + 1.6 = 301.6 m³.

Step 5: Compute net volume of air remaining:
V_air = V_total - Total occupied volume
V_air = 984.375 - 301.6 = 682.775 m³ ≈ 682.78 m³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
840 + 144.375 = 984.375 m³. Occupied = 301.6 m³. Net air = 682.775 m³.
Boxed Answer: [ Total = 984.38 m³, Air Available = 682.78 m³ ].

worked_examples.given: Cylindrical glass: inner diameter d = 5 cm ⇒ radius r = 2.5 cm. Height h = 10 cm. Raised hemispherical bottom of radius r = 2.5 cm (Fig. 12.13). Use π = 3.14.
worked_examples.formula:
Apparent capacity = Volume of cylinder = πr²h.
Volume of hemispherical bump = (2/3)πr³.
Actual capacity = Apparent capacity - Volume of hemisphere = πr²h - (2/3)πr³ = πr²[h - (2/3)r].
worked_examples.calculation:
Apparent capacity = 196.25 cm³.
Actual capacity = 163.54 cm³.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Apparent capacity = 196.25 cm³, Actual capacity = 163.54 cm³
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Inner diameter of the cylindrical glass, d = 5 cm.
Radius, r = 5 / 2 = 2.5 cm.
Height of the glass, h = 10 cm.
Raised hemispherical bottom with radius r = 2.5 cm.
Use π = 3.14 (Fig. 12.13).

TO FIND:
(i) Apparent capacity of the glass.
(ii) Actual capacity of the glass.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Apparent Capacity (Volume of Cylinder):
V_apparent = πr²h
V_apparent = 3.14 × (2.5)² × 10
V_apparent = 3.14 × 6.25 × 10
V_apparent = 3.14 × 62.5 = 196.25 cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of the raised hemispherical bottom:
V_hemisphere = (2 / 3) × πr³
V_hemisphere = (2 / 3) × 3.14 × (2.5)³
V_hemisphere = (2 / 3) × 3.14 × 15.625
V_hemisphere = 98.125 / 3 ≈ 32.71 cm³.

Step 3: Compute Actual Capacity:
V_actual = V_apparent - V_hemisphere
V_actual = 196.25 - 32.71 = 163.54 cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
Cylinder: 3.14 × 62.5 = 196.25 cm³. Hemisphere: (2/3) × 3.14 × 15.625 = 32.708 cm³. Net = 196.25 - 32.71 = 163.54 cm³.
Boxed Answer: [ Apparent = 196.25 cm³, Actual = 163.54 cm³ ].

Right circular cylinder circumscribes toy: radius R = 2 cm, height H = cone height + hemisphere radius = 2 + 2 = 4 cm. Use π = 3.14.
worked_examples.formula:
Volume of toy = Volume of cone + Volume of hemisphere = (1/3)πr²h + (2/3)πr³ = (1/3)πr²(h + 2r).
Volume of cylinder = πr²H.
Difference = Volume of cylinder - Volume of toy.
worked_examples.calculation:
Volume of toy = 25.12 cm³.
Volume of cylinder = 50.24 cm³.
Difference = 25.12 cm³.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Volume of toy = 25.12 cm³, Difference = 25.12 cm³
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A toy in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a right circular cone.
Base diameter, d = 4 cm ⇒ radius, r = 2 cm.
Height of the cone, h = 2 cm.
Radius of hemisphere, r = 2 cm.
A cylinder circumscribes the toy:
Radius of cylinder, r = 2 cm.
Height of cylinder, H = cone height + hemisphere radius = 2 + 2 = 4 cm.
Use π = 3.14 (Fig. 12.14).

TO FIND:
(i) Volume of the toy.
(ii) Difference between the volumes of the cylinder and the toy.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Volume of the Toy:
Volume of toy = Volume of cone + Volume of hemisphere
V_toy = (1 / 3)πr²h + (2 / 3)πr³
V_toy = (1 / 3)πr² (h + 2r)
V_toy = (1 / 3) × 3.14 × 2² × [ 2 + 2(2) ]
V_toy = (1 / 3) × 3.14 × 4 × 6
V_toy = 2 × 4 × 3.14 = 8 × 3.14 = 25.12 cm³.

Step 2: Compute Volume of the Circumscribing Cylinder:
V_cylinder = πr²H
V_cylinder = 3.14 × 2² × 4
V_cylinder = 3.14 × 16 = 50.24 cm³.

Step 3: Compute Difference in Volumes:
Difference = V_cylinder - V_toy
Difference = 50.24 - 25.12 = 25.12 cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
Toy volume = 25.12 cm³. Cylinder volume = 50.24 cm³. Notice V_cylinder = 2 × V_toy, so the difference is exactly 25.12 cm³!
Boxed Answer: [ Volume of Toy = 25.12 cm³, Difference = 25.12 cm³ ].

In surface area calculations of joined solids, why do we exclude the contact base areas between the cylinder and hemispheres?

title: Exercise 12.1 Complete Solver: Joined Cubes, Surmounted Solids & Canvas Tents (Q1 to Q9)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 12.1 Questions 1 through 9. Covers cubes joined end to end (Q1), hollow cylinder on hollow hemisphere (Q2), cone on hemisphere toy (Q3), cubical block with hemisphere (Q4 & Q5), 14 mm medicine capsule (Q6), conical tent on cylinder (Q7), conical cavity hollowed from solid cylinder (Q8), and wooden cylinder with hemispherical scoops (Q9).
key_concepts: Ex 12.1 Q1: Two cubes volume 64 cm³ ⇒ Edge a = 4 cm; Joined cuboid: L = 8 cm, B = 4 cm, H = 4 cm ⇒ TSA = 2(32 + 16 + 32) = 160 cm²
Ex 12.1 Q2: Vessel: Hemisphere d = 14 cm (r = 7 cm), Total H = 13 cm ⇒ Cylinder h = 13 - 7 = 6 cm ⇒ Inner SA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r) = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 13 = 572 cm²
Ex 12.1 Q3: Toy: r = 3.5 cm, Total H = 15.5 cm ⇒ Cone h = 12 cm, l = √(12² + 3.5²) = 12.5 cm ⇒ TSA = πrl + 2πr² = 214.5 cm²
Ex 12.1 Q4: Block side 7 cm: Greatest hemisphere d = 7 cm (r = 3.5 cm) ⇒ TSA = 6(49) + π(3.5)² = 294 + 38.5 = 332.5 cm²
Ex 12.1 Q5: Hemispherical depression edge l: TSA = 6l² + π(l/2)² = (l²/4)(24 + π)
Ex 12.1 Q6: Capsule length 14 mm, diameter 5 mm (r = 2.5 mm): Cylinder h = 14 - 5 = 9 mm ⇒ TSA = 2πr(h + 2r) = 2 × (22/7) × 2.5 × 14 = 220 mm²
Ex 12.1 Q7: Tent: Cylinder d = 4 m (r = 2 m), h = 2.1 m; Cone l = 2.8 m ⇒ Canvas = 2πrh + πrl = πr(2h + l) = (22/7) × 2 × (4.2 + 2.8) = 44 m²; Cost at ₹500/m² = ₹22000
Ex 12.1 Q8: Cylinder h = 2.4 cm, d = 1.4 cm (r = 0.7 cm), cone l = √(2.4² + 0.7²) = 2.5 cm ⇒ Remaining TSA = 2πrh + πr² + πrl = 17.6 cm² ≈ 18 cm²
Ex 12.1 Q9: Wooden cylinder h = 10 cm, r = 3.5 cm with 2 scoops: TSA = 2πrh + 2(2πr²) = 2πr(h + 2r) = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × (10 + 7) = 374 cm²

Factoring out 2πr to save 80% calculation time
Nearest whole integer rounding in board exams

worked_examples.problem: [NCERT Class 10 Ch 12 | Section 12.1 | Page 165] Exercise 12.1 Q1: 2 cubes each of volume 64 cm³ are joined end to end. Find the surface area of the resulting cuboid.
worked_examples.section: 12.1 Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
worked_examples.image_search_query: two cubes joined cuboid surface area
worked_examples.given: Two cubes each of volume V = 64 cm³ joined end to end.
worked_examples.formula: Volume of cube = a³ ⇒ a = V^(1/3). Dimensions of resulting cuboid: length L = 2a, breadth B = a, height H = a. Surface area of cuboid = 2(LB + BH + HL).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Two identical cubes, each having volume V = 64 cm³, are joined end to end.

TO FIND:
Surface area of the resulting cuboid.

FORMULA USED:
- Volume of a cube = a³, where a is the side length.
- Surface area of a cuboid = 2(LB + BH + HL).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Find the edge length a of each cube:
a³ = 64
a = ∛64 = 4 cm.

Step 2: Determine dimensions of the resulting cuboid:
When two cubes are joined end to end:
Length, L = 4 + 4 = 8 cm
Breadth, B = 4 cm
Height, H = 4 cm.

Step 3: Calculate the surface area of the cuboid:
Surface Area = 2(LB + BH + HL)
= 2( (8 × 4) + (4 × 4) + (4 × 8) )
= 2( 32 + 16 + 32 )
= 2( 80 ) = 160 cm².

worked_examples.given: Vessel: hollow hemisphere mounted by hollow cylinder. Hemisphere diameter d = 14 cm ⇒ radius r = 7 cm. Total height H = 13 cm. Cylinder height h = 13 - 7 = 6 cm. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula: Inner surface area = Inner CSA of cylinder + Inner CSA of hemisphere = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A hollow hemisphere mounted by a hollow cylinder.
Diameter of the hemisphere, d = 14 cm ⇒ radius, r = 7 cm.
Total height of the vessel, H = 13 cm.
Height of the cylindrical portion, h = H - r = 13 - 7 = 6 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Inner surface area of the vessel.

FORMULA USED:
Inner surface area = Curved surface area of cylinder + Curved surface area of hemisphere
Area = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Determine the height of the cylinder:
h = 13 - 7 = 6 cm.

Step 2: Apply the combined formula:
Area = 2πr (h + r)
Area = 2 × (22 / 7) × 7 × (6 + 7)
Cancel 7 in numerator and denominator:
Area = 44 × 13
44 × 13 = 44 × 10 + 44 × 3 = 440 + 132 = 572 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
CSA cylinder = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 7 × 6 = 264 cm². CSA hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 308 cm². Sum = 264 + 308 = 572 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 572 cm² ].

worked_examples.given: Toy: cone mounted on hemisphere. Radius r = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm. Total height H = 15.5 cm. Height of cone h = 15.5 - 3.5 = 12 cm. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Slant height of cone l = √(r² + h²).
Total surface area of toy = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere = πrl + 2πr² = πr(l + 2r).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A toy in the form of a cone mounted on a hemisphere of the same radius.
Radius of hemisphere and cone, r = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm.
Total height of the toy, H = 15.5 cm.
Height of conical part, h = H - r = 15.5 - 3.5 = 12 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Total surface area of the toy.

FORMULA USED:
Total surface area = CSA of cone + CSA of hemisphere = πrl + 2πr² = πr(l + 2r)
where slant height l = √(r² + h²).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute slant height l of the cone:
l = √(r² + h²) = √(3.5² + 12²) = √(12.25 + 144) = √156.25 = 12.5 cm.

Step 2: Calculate Total Surface Area:
TSA = πr (l + 2r)
TSA = (22 / 7) × (7 / 2) × [ 12.5 + 2(3.5) ]
TSA = 11 × [ 12.5 + 7 ]
TSA = 11 × 19.5 = 214.5 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
CSA cone = (22/7) × 3.5 × 12.5 = 11 × 12.5 = 137.5 cm². CSA hemisphere = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5² = 77 cm². Total = 137.5 + 77 = 214.5 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 214.5 cm² ].

worked_examples.given: Cubical block edge a = 7 cm. A hemisphere is surmounted on top face of cube. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
The greatest diameter of hemisphere = edge length of cube = a = 7 cm ⇒ radius r = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm.
Surface Area of solid = TSA of cube - Base area of hemisphere + CSA of hemisphere = 6a² + πr².
worked_examples.calculation:
Greatest diameter = 7 cm.
Surface Area = 332.5 cm².
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Greatest diameter = 7 cm, Surface area = 332.5 cm²
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Side of the cubical block, a = 7 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
(i) Greatest diameter the hemisphere can have.
(ii) Surface area of the resulting solid.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Find greatest diameter of the hemisphere:
The circular base of the hemisphere lies on the top square face of the cube. The maximum diameter cannot exceed the side length of the square face:
Greatest Diameter = a = 7 cm.
Radius, r = 7 / 2 = 3.5 cm.

Step 2: Formula for Surface Area of Solid:
Surface Area = Total surface area of cube - Base area of hemisphere + CSA of hemisphere
Area = 6a² - πr² + 2πr²
Area = 6a² + πr².

Step 3: Calculate numerical values:
Area_cube = 6a² = 6 × 7² = 6 × 49 = 294 cm².
Net hemisphere addition = πr² = (22 / 7) × (7 / 2)² = (22 / 7) × (49 / 4) = 77 / 2 = 38.5 cm².
Total Surface Area = 294 + 38.5 = 332.5 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
294 + 38.5 = 332.5 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ Greatest diameter = 7 cm, Surface Area = 332.5 cm² ].

worked_examples.problem: [NCERT Class 10 Ch 12 | Section 12.1 | Page 166] Exercise 12.1 Q5: A hemispherical depression is cut out from one face of a cubical wooden block such that the diameter l of the hemisphere is equal to the edge of the cube. Determine the surface area of the remaining solid.
worked_examples.section: 12.1 Surface Area of a Combination of Solids
worked_examples.image_search_query: hemispherical depression cut cubical block surface area
worked_examples.given: Cubical block edge = l. Hemispherical depression diameter = l ⇒ radius r = l / 2.
worked_examples.formula: Surface area of remaining solid = Total surface area of cube - Circular top opening + Curved surface area of hemispherical cavity = 6l² - πr² + 2πr² = 6l² + πr².
worked_examples.substitution:
r = l / 2 ⇒ r² = l² / 4.
Surface Area = 6l² + π(l² / 4) = (l² / 4)(24 + π).
worked_examples.calculation: Surface Area = (1/4) l² (24 + π) sq units.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Edge length of the cubical wooden block = l.
Diameter of the hemispherical depression = l.
Radius of the hemisphere, r = l / 2.

TO FIND:
Surface area of the remaining solid.

FORMULA USED:
When a hemispherical cavity is carved out from a face of the cube:
1. The top flat face loses a circular area of πr².
2. A new curved inner surface of the hemispherical bowl is created, adding 2πr².
Surface Area = Total Surface Area of cube - Base area of hemisphere + Curved surface area of hemisphere
Area = 6l² - πr² + 2πr² = 6l² + πr².

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute r = l / 2 into the expression:
Area = 6l² + π (l / 2)²
Area = 6l² + π (l² / 4)

Step 2: Factor out l² / 4:
Area = (24l² / 4) + (πl² / 4)
Area = (l² / 4) (24 + π) square units.

[ROUGH_WORK]
6 + π/4 = (24 + π)/4. Multiplying by l² gives (1/4)l²(24 + π).
Boxed Answer: [ (1/4) l² (24 + π) sq units ].

worked_examples.formula: Total Surface Area = CSA of cylinder + 2 × CSA of hemisphere = 2πrh + 2 × (2πr²) = 2πr(h + 2r).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A medicine capsule consisting of a cylinder with two hemispheres attached at both ends.
Total length of the capsule = 14 mm.
Diameter of the capsule, d = 5 mm ⇒ radius, r = 2.5 mm = 5/2 mm.
Length of the cylindrical part, h = 14 - 2(r) = 14 - 2(2.5) = 14 - 5 = 9 mm.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.10).

TO FIND:
Surface area of the capsule.

FORMULA USED:
Total surface area = CSA of cylinder + 2 × CSA of hemisphere
Area = 2πrh + 2 × (2πr²) = 2πrh + 4πr² = 2πr(h + 2r).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute parameters into formula:
Area = 2 × (22 / 7) × (5 / 2) × [ 9 + 2(5 / 2) ]
Area = (22 / 7) × 5 × [ 9 + 5 ]
Area = (22 / 7) × 5 × 14

Step 2: Simplify by dividing 14 by 7:
14 / 7 = 2
Area = 22 × 5 × 2
Area = 22 × 10 = 220 mm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
2πr(h + 2r) = 2 × (22/7) × 2.5 × 14 = 2 × 22 × 2.5 × 2 = 220 mm².
Boxed Answer: [ 220 mm² ].

worked_examples.given: Tent: cylinder surmounted by conical top. Cylinder height h = 2.1 m, diameter d = 4 m ⇒ radius r = 2 m. Slant height of cone l = 2.8 m. Canvas rate = ₹ 500 per m². Base of tent is open (no canvas). Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Area of canvas = CSA of cylinder + CSA of cone = 2πrh + πrl = πr(2h + l).
Cost = Area × Rate.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A tent in the shape of a cylinder surmounted by a cone.
Height of the cylinder, h = 2.1 m.
Diameter of the cylindrical base, d = 4 m ⇒ radius, r = 2 m.
Slant height of the conical roof, l = 2.8 m.
Rate of canvas = ₹ 500 per m².
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
(i) Area of canvas used for making the tent.
(ii) Total cost of the canvas.

FORMULA USED:
Since the tent floor is not covered with canvas:
Area of canvas = CSA of cylinder + CSA of cone
Area = 2πrh + πrl = πr(2h + l).
Total Cost = Area × Rate.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute Area of canvas:
Area = πr (2h + l)
Area = (22 / 7) × 2 × [ 2(2.1) + 2.8 ]
Area = (44 / 7) × [ 4.2 + 2.8 ]
Area = (44 / 7) × 7.0
Cancel 7:
Area = 44 m².

Step 2: Calculate Total Cost:
Cost = Area × Rate
Cost = 44 × ₹ 500 = ₹ 22,000.

[ROUGH_WORK]
2h + l = 4.2 + 2.8 = 7. (22/7) × 2 × 7 = 44 m². 44 × 500 = 22000 rupees.
Boxed Answer: [ Area = 44 m², Cost = ₹ 22,000 ].

worked_examples.given: Solid cylinder height h = 2.4 cm, diameter d = 1.4 cm ⇒ radius r = 0.7 cm. Conical cavity scooped out has same height h = 2.4 cm and radius r = 0.7 cm. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Total Surface Area of remaining solid = CSA of cylinder + Area of top flat base of cylinder + Inner CSA of conical cavity
TSA = 2πrh + πr² + πrl = πr(2h + r + l)
where slant height l = √(r² + h²).
worked_examples.finalAnswer: 17.6 cm² (or 18 cm² to the nearest cm²)
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A solid cylinder of height h = 2.4 cm and diameter d = 1.4 cm.
Radius, r = 1.4 / 2 = 0.7 cm.
A conical cavity of the same height h = 2.4 cm and same radius r = 0.7 cm is hollowed out.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Total surface area of the remaining solid to the nearest cm².

FORMULA USED:
When the conical cavity is scooped out:
- The outer curved cylinder surface is intact: 2πrh
- One flat circular base is intact: πr²
- The internal conical hollow is exposed: πrl
Total Surface Area = 2πrh + πr² + πrl = πr(2h + r + l)
where slant height l = √(r² + h²).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute slant height l of the conical cavity:
l = √(r² + h²) = √(0.7² + 2.4²) = √(0.49 + 5.76) = √6.25 = 2.5 cm.

Step 2: Calculate Total Surface Area:
TSA = πr (2h + r + l)
TSA = (22 / 7) × 0.7 × [ 2(2.4) + 0.7 + 2.5 ]
TSA = 2.2 × [ 4.8 + 0.7 + 2.5 ]
TSA = 2.2 × 8.0 = 17.6 cm².

Step 3: Round to the nearest cm²:
17.6 cm² rounded to the nearest integer is 18 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
2.2 × 8 = 17.6 cm². Nearest whole number is 18 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 17.6 cm² (or 18 cm² to nearest cm²) ].

worked_examples.given: Solid cylinder with height h = 10 cm and radius r = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm. A hemisphere of radius r = 3.5 cm is scooped out from each of the two ends (Fig. 12.11). Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula: Total Surface Area = CSA of cylinder + 2 × CSA of hemisphere = 2πrh + 2(2πr²) = 2πr(h + 2r).
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A wooden article made by scooping out a hemisphere from each end of a solid cylinder.
Height of cylinder, h = 10 cm.
Radius of cylinder and hemispherical cavities, r = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.11).

TO FIND:
Total surface area of the article.

FORMULA USED:
Total surface area = CSA of cylinder + 2 × CSA of hemisphere
Area = 2πrh + 2 × (2πr²) = 2πrh + 4πr² = 2πr(h + 2r).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute parameters into formula:
Area = 2πr (h + 2r)
Area = 2 × (22 / 7) × (7 / 2) × [ 10 + 2(3.5) ]
Area = 22 × [ 10 + 7 ]
Area = 22 × 17

Step 2: Compute product:
22 × 17 = 22 × 10 + 22 × 7 = 220 + 154 = 374 cm².

[ROUGH_WORK]
CSA cylinder = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 10 = 220 cm². Two hemispheres = 4 × (22/7) × 3.5² = 154 cm². Total = 220 + 154 = 374 cm².
Boxed Answer: [ 374 cm² ].

In surface area calculations of joined solids, why do we exclude the contact base areas between the cylinder and hemispheres?

common_misconceptions: Subtracting 2.5 mm instead of 5 mm from total length: There are TWO hemispheres at the ends, so subtract 2 × 2.5 = 5 mm!
Including the floor in the tent calculation: Exercise 12.1 Q7 explicitly states 'the base of the tent will not be covered with canvas'.

title: Exercise 12.2 Part 1 Solver: Solid Combinations, Cones, Cylinders, Gulab Jamuns & Pen Stands (Q1 to Q4)
description: Complete step-by-step resolution of NCERT Exercise 12.2 Questions 1 through 8. Covers cone on hemisphere volume in terms of π (Q1), Rachel's model cylinder with 2 cones (Q2), 45 gulab jamuns 30% syrup volume (Q3), pen stand with 4 conical depressions (Q4), inverted cone with 100 lead shots dropping 1/4 water (Q5), solid iron pole mass (Q6), upright solid inside cylinder (Q7), and checking student's sphere-cylinder vessel volume calculation (Q8).
key_concepts: Ex 12.2 Q2: Model d = 3 cm (r = 1.5 cm), L = 12 cm, cone h = 2 cm ⇒ Cylinder h = 8 cm ⇒ V = πr²(h_cyl + 2/3 h_cone) = 66 cm³
Ex 12.2 Q3: Gulab jamun d = 2.8 cm (r = 1.4 cm), L = 5 cm ⇒ Cyl h = 2.2 cm ⇒ 1 Jamun V = 25.05 cm³; 45 Jamuns = 1127.28 cm³ ⇒ 30% syrup = 338.18 cm³ ≈ 338 cm³
Ex 12.2 Q4: Cuboid 15×10×3.5 = 525 cm³; 4 cones r = 0.5 cm, h = 1.4 cm ⇒ 4(1/3 πr²h) = 1.47 cm³ ⇒ Remaining wood = 523.53 cm³
Ex 12.2 Q5: Inverted cone r = 5 cm, h = 8 cm: V = 200π/3 cm³; 1/4 flows out = 50π/3 cm³; Sphere r = 0.5 cm: V = 4/3 π(1/8) = π/6 cm³ ⇒ n = (50π/3) / (π/6) = 100 lead shots!
Ex 12.2 Q6: Iron pole: Base cylinder r = 12 cm, h = 220 cm; Top cylinder r = 8 cm, h = 60 cm ⇒ V = 111532.8 cm³; Mass = 111532.8 × 8 g = 892.26 kg
Ex 12.2 Q7: Cylinder r = 60 cm, H = 180 cm: V = 648000π; Solid = 288000π ⇒ Water left = 360000π cm³ = 1.131 m³
Ex 12.2 Q8: Spherical vessel r = 4.25 cm, neck r = 1 cm, h = 8 cm: V = 321.39 + 25.12 = 346.51 cm³ (Student's answer 345 cm³ is incorrect!)
subtopics: Full resolution of Exercise 12.2 Questions 1 to 8
Sugar syrup percentage computation across 45 units
Archimedes principle lead shot integer counting

worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A solid consisting of a cone standing on a hemisphere.
Radius of hemisphere and cone, r = 1 cm.
Height of the cone, h = r = 1 cm.

TO FIND:
Volume of the solid in terms of π.

FORMULA USED:
Volume of solid = Volume of cone + Volume of hemisphere
V = (1 / 3)πr²h + (2 / 3)πr³ = (1 / 3)πr²(h + 2r).

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute r = 1 cm and h = 1 cm:
V = (1 / 3) × π × 1² × [ 1 + 2(1) ]
V = (1 / 3) × π × 1 × [ 1 + 2 ]
V = (1 / 3) × π × 3
V = π cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
(1/3)π + (2/3)π = π cm³.
Boxed Answer: [ π cm³ ].

worked_examples.given: Model: cylinder with 2 identical cones at ends. Diameter d = 3 cm ⇒ radius r = 1.5 cm = 3/2 cm. Total length L = 12 cm. Each cone height h_cone = 2 cm. Cylinder height h_cyl = 12 - 2(2) = 8 cm. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula: Volume of model = Volume of cylinder + 2 × Volume of cone = πr² h_cyl + 2 × [(1/3)πr² h_cone] = πr² [h_cyl + (2/3) h_cone].
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A model made of a central cylinder with two identical cones attached at each end.
Diameter of model, d = 3 cm ⇒ radius, r = 1.5 cm = 3/2 cm.
Total length of model, L = 12 cm.
Height of each cone, h_cone = 2 cm.
Height of cylinder, h_cyl = 12 - 2(h_cone) = 12 - 2(2) = 8 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Volume of air contained in the model.

FORMULA USED:
Total Volume = Volume of cylinder + 2 × Volume of cone
V = πr² h_cyl + 2 × [ (1 / 3) πr² h_cone ] = πr² [ h_cyl + (2 / 3) h_cone ].

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Substitute parameters into formula:
V = (22 / 7) × (3 / 2)² × [ 8 + (2 / 3)(2) ]
V = (22 / 7) × (9 / 4) × [ 8 + 4 / 3 ]
V = (22 / 7) × (9 / 4) × (28 / 3)

Step 2: Simplify fractions:
Notice that 7 × 4 in denominator = 28, which cancels exactly with 28 in numerator!
Also 9 / 3 = 3.
V = 22 × 3 × 1 = 66 cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
Cylinder volume = (22/7) × 2.25 × 8 = 56.57 cm³. Two cones = 2 × (1/3) × (22/7) × 2.25 × 2 = 9.43 cm³. Sum = 56.57 + 9.43 = 66 cm³.
Boxed Answer: [ 66 cm³ ].

worked_examples.given: Shape: cylinder with 2 hemispherical ends (Fig. 12.15). Total length L = 5 cm. Diameter d = 2.8 cm ⇒ radius r = 1.4 cm. Cylinder length h = 5 - 2(1.4) = 5 - 2.8 = 2.2 cm. Number of gulab jamuns = 45. Syrup percentage = 30%. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Volume of 1 gulab jamun = Volume of cylinder + Volume of two hemispheres (sphere) = πr²h + (4/3)πr³ = πr²[h + (4/3)r].
Total volume of 45 gulab jamuns = 45 × Volume of 1.
Syrup volume = 30% of Total Volume = 0.30 × Total Volume.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Shape of each gulab jamun: cylinder with two hemispherical ends.
Total length of gulab jamun, L = 5 cm.
Diameter, d = 2.8 cm ⇒ radius, r = 1.4 cm.
Length of cylindrical portion, h = 5 - 2(1.4) = 5 - 2.8 = 2.2 cm.
Number of gulab jamuns = 45.
Syrup content = 30% of total volume.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.15).

TO FIND:
Total volume of sugar syrup in 45 gulab jamuns.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of one gulab jamun:
Volume = Volume of cylinder + Volume of two hemispheres (one complete sphere)
V_1 = πr²h + (4 / 3)πr³
V_1 = πr² [ h + (4 / 3)r ]
V_1 = (22 / 7) × (1.4)² × [ 2.2 + (4 / 3) × 1.4 ]
V_1 = (22 / 7) × 1.96 × [ 2.2 + 5.6 / 3 ]
Since 1.96 / 7 = 0.28:
V_1 = (22 × 0.28) × [ (6.6 + 5.6) / 3 ]
V_1 = 6.16 × (12.2 / 3) = 75.152 / 3 ≈ 25.05 cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of 45 gulab jamuns:
V_45 = 45 × V_1 = 45 × (75.152 / 3) = 15 × 75.152 = 1127.28 cm³.

Step 3: Compute syrup volume (30% of total):
V_syrup = 30% of 1127.28
V_syrup = (30 / 100) × 1127.28 = 0.3 × 1127.28 = 338.18 cm³ ≈ 338 cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
45 × (75.152/3) × 0.3 = 15 × 75.152 × 0.3 = 4.5 × 75.152 = 338.18 cm³.
Boxed Answer: [ 338 cm³ (approx) ].

worked_examples.formula: Volume of wood in stand = Volume of cuboid - 4 × Volume of one conical depression = (l × b × h) - 4 × [(1/3)πr²h'].
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A wooden cuboid of dimensions: length l = 15 cm, breadth b = 10 cm, height h = 3.5 cm.
4 identical conical depressions, each with radius r = 0.5 cm and depth h' = 1.4 cm.
Use π = 22/7 (Fig. 12.16).

TO FIND:
Volume of wood in the entire stand.

FORMULA USED:
Volume of wood = Volume of cuboid - 4 × Volume of one conical depression
V = (l × b × h) - 4 × [ (1 / 3) πr² h' ].

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of the cuboid:
V_cuboid = 15 × 10 × 3.5 = 525 cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of the 4 conical depressions:
V_depressions = 4 × [ (1 / 3) × (22 / 7) × (0.5)² × 1.4 ]
V_depressions = 4 × [ (1 / 3) × (22 / 7) × 0.25 × 1.4 ]
Since 1.4 / 7 = 0.2:
V_depressions = 4 × (1 / 3) × 22 × (0.25 × 0.2)
V_depressions = 4 × (1 / 3) × 22 × 0.05
V_depressions = (4 × 1.1) / 3 = 4.4 / 3 ≈ 1.467 cm³.

Step 3: Subtract from cuboid volume:
V_wood = 525 - 1.467 = 523.533... ≈ 523.53 cm³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
525 - 1.47 = 523.53 cm³.
Boxed Answer: [ 523.53 cm³ ].

What happens if the depth of a conical depression exceeds the height of the cuboid?

title: Exercise 12.2 Part 2 Solver: Inverted Cones, Lead Shots, Iron Poles & Spherical Vessels (Q5 to Q8)
description: Master real-world industrial and physical applications of surface areas and volumes: computing iron pole mass using density (Mass = Volume × Density), structural canvas requirements, packaging optimization, and verifying complex container capacities with rigorous dimensional checks.
key_concepts: Density to Mass Conversion: Mass = Volume × Density (e.g. 1 cm³ of iron = 8 g ⇒ Mass in kg = Volume × 8 / 1000)
Structural Compound Models: Rachel's engineering rocket model (Cylinder with conical nose and tail)
Dimensional Consistency Check: Volume is cubic units (cm³, m³), Surface area is square units (cm², m²); 1 m³ = 1,000,000 cm³ = 1000 Litres
Ratio of Shapes: Sphere inscribed in a cylinder has Volume(Sphere) : Volume(Cylinder) = 2 : 3 and SA(Sphere) : TSA(Cylinder) = 2 : 3 (Archimedes' tombstone theorem!)
subtopics: Metric conversions between cm³, m³, and litres

worked_examples.given: Inverted cone: height H = 8 cm, top radius R = 5 cm. Filled with water. Lead shots: spheres of radius r = 0.5 cm. Water overflowing = (1/4) of total vessel volume.
worked_examples.formula: Number of lead shots n = Volume of water overflowing / Volume of 1 lead shot = [(1/4) × (1/3)πR²H] / [(4/3)πr³].
worked_examples.substitution:
Volume of water in cone = (1/3)π × 5² × 8 = 200π / 3 cm³.
Volume of water displaced = (1/4) × (200π / 3) = 50π / 3 cm³.
Volume of 1 lead shot = (4/3)π × (0.5)³ = (4/3)π × 0.125 = 0.5π / 3 cm³ = π / 6 cm³.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
An inverted cone with height H = 8 cm and base radius R = 5 cm, filled to the brim with water.
Lead shots are spheres of radius r = 0.5 cm.
Fraction of water overflowing when lead shots are dropped = 1/4.

TO FIND:
The number of lead shots dropped into the vessel.

FORMULA USED:
By Archimedes' Principle, the volume of water displaced and overflowing equals the total volume of all dropped submerged lead shots:
n × Volume of 1 lead shot = (1 / 4) × Volume of cone
n × [ (4 / 3) πr³ ] = (1 / 4) × [ (1 / 3) πR² H ].

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of the cone:
V_cone = (1 / 3) π R² H
V_cone = (1 / 3) × π × 5² × 8 = (200 / 3) π cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of water displaced:
V_displaced = (1 / 4) × V_cone
V_displaced = (1 / 4) × (200 / 3) π = (50 / 3) π cm³.

Step 3: Compute volume of 1 spherical lead shot:
V_shot = (4 / 3) π r³
V_shot = (4 / 3) × π × (0.5)³
V_shot = (4 / 3) × π × 0.125 = (0.5 / 3) π cm³.

Step 4: Solve for number of lead shots n:
n = V_displaced / V_shot
n = [ (50 / 3) π ] / [ (0.5 / 3) π ]
Cancel π and 3 from numerator and denominator:
n = 50 / 0.5 = 100.

[ROUGH_WORK]
50 / 0.5 = 100 lead shots.
Boxed Answer: [ 100 lead shots ].
concept_questions: How does Archimedes' principle connect the volume of submerged lead spheres to the volume of water displaced?
Why is the fraction of displaced water equal to the ratio: (n × volume of 1 sphere) / (volume of cone)?

worked_examples.formula:
Total volume of pole = Volume of lower cylinder + Volume of upper cylinder = π R1² H1 + π R2² H2 = π [R1² H1 + R2² H2].
Mass = Volume × Density.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
Lower cylinder: height H1 = 220 cm, radius R1 = 24 / 2 = 12 cm.
Upper cylinder: height H2 = 60 cm, radius R2 = 8 cm.
Density of iron = 8 g per cm³.
Use π = 3.14.

TO FIND:
Mass of the solid iron pole in kilograms.

FORMULA USED:
Total Volume = Volume of lower cylinder + Volume of upper cylinder
V = π R1² H1 + π R2² H2 = π [ R1² H1 + R2² H2 ].
Mass = Volume × Density.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute total volume of iron:
V = 3.14 × [ (12)² × 220 + (8)² × 60 ]
V = 3.14 × [ (144 × 220) + (64 × 60) ]
V = 3.14 × [ 31680 + 3840 ]
V = 3.14 × 35520 = 111532.8 cm³.

Step 2: Calculate mass in grams:
Mass = 111532.8 cm³ × 8 g/cm³ = 892262.4 g.

Step 3: Convert mass to kilograms:
Mass in kg = 892262.4 / 1000 = 892.2624 kg ≈ 892.26 kg.

[ROUGH_WORK]
35520 × 3.14 = 111532.8 cm³. 111532.8 × 8 = 892262.4 g = 892.26 kg.
Boxed Answer: [ 892.26 kg ].

worked_examples.given: Solid: cone (h = 120 cm, r = 60 cm) on hemisphere (r = 60 cm). Cylinder: radius R = 60 cm, height H = 180 cm. Full of water. Use π = 22/7.
worked_examples.formula:
Volume of water left = Volume of cylinder - Volume of submerged solid
Volume of solid = Volume of cone + Volume of hemisphere = (1/3)πr²h + (2/3)πr³.
Volume of cylinder = πR²H.
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A solid consisting of a cone standing on a hemisphere:
Radius of cone and hemisphere, r = 60 cm.
Height of the cone, h = 120 cm.
A cylinder full of water:
Radius of cylinder, R = 60 cm.
Height of cylinder, H = 180 cm.
Use π = 22/7.

TO FIND:
Volume of water left in the cylinder after the solid is submerged.

FORMULA USED:
Volume of water left = Volume of cylinder - Volume of submerged solid
where:
- Volume of cylinder = πR²H
- Volume of solid = Volume of cone + Volume of hemisphere = (1/3)πr²h + (2/3)πr³

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of the submerged solid:
Since r = 60 cm:
V_solid = (1 / 3) π r² [ h + 2r ]
V_solid = (1 / 3) π (60)² [ 120 + 2(60) ]
V_solid = (1 / 3) π × 3600 × [ 120 + 120 ]
V_solid = 1200 π × 240 = 288000 π cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of the full cylinder of water:
V_cylinder = π R² H
V_cylinder = π × (60)² × 180
V_cylinder = 3600 × 180 × π = 648000 π cm³.

Step 3: Compute volume of water left:
V_left = V_cylinder - V_solid
V_left = 648000 π - 288000 π = 360000 π cm³.

Step 4: Substitute π = 22/7 and convert to m³:
V_left = 360000 × (22 / 7) = 7920000 / 7 ≈ 1131428.57 cm³.
Convert to cubic metres (1 m³ = 10⁶ cm³):
V_left = 1131428.57 / 1000000 ≈ 1.131 m³.

[ROUGH_WORK]
648000π - 288000π = 360000π. 360000 × 22/7 = 1131428.57 cm³ = 1.131 m³.
Boxed Answer: [ 1.131 m³ (or 1.13 m³) ].

In surface area calculations of joined solids, why do we exclude the contact base areas between the cylinder and hemispheres?

worked_examples.formula: Actual volume = Volume of cylinder + Volume of sphere = πr²h + (4/3)πR³.
worked_examples.calculation: Total volume = 346.51 cm³. Child's claim (345 cm³) is incorrect.
worked_examples.finalAnswer: Total volume = 346.51 cm³, Child is incorrect (Correct volume is 346.51 cm³)
worked_examples.solution:
GIVEN:
A glass vessel consisting of a spherical body with a cylindrical neck.
Cylindrical neck: height h = 8 cm, radius r = 2 / 2 = 1 cm.
Spherical body: radius R = 8.5 / 2 = 4.25 cm.
Child's measured volume = 345 cm³.
Use π = 3.14.

TO FIND:
Check whether the child is correct by computing the exact inside volume.

FORMULA USED:
Total Volume = Volume of cylindrical neck + Volume of spherical body
V = πr²h + (4 / 3)πR³.

STEP-BY-STEP CALCULATION:
Step 1: Compute volume of the cylindrical neck:
V_cylinder = πr²h
V_cylinder = 3.14 × 1² × 8 = 25.12 cm³.

Step 2: Compute volume of the spherical body:
V_sphere = (4 / 3) π R³
V_sphere = (4 / 3) × 3.14 × (4.25)³
(4.25)³ = 76.765625
V_sphere = (4 / 3) × 3.14 × 76.765625
V_sphere = (4 / 3) × 241.0440625 ≈ 321.392 cm³.

Step 3: Compute total internal volume:
V_total = V_cylinder + V_sphere
V_total = 25.12 + 321.392 = 346.512 cm³ ≈ 346.51 cm³.

Step 4: Verify child's measurement:
The child found the volume to be 345 cm³.
Since the actual calculated volume is 346.51 cm³, the child's measurement is incorrect.

[ROUGH_WORK]
25.12 + 321.39 = 346.51 cm³. 345 ≠ 346.51, so she is incorrect!
Boxed Answer: [ Child is Incorrect; Correct Volume = 346.51 cm³ ].
